messages:
jamie: Heads-up from GTM: a few EU customers are asking for an explicit opt-in that routes them to a cost-optimized quantized model during peak hours. They want a clear canary + rollback ladder before we promise any cutover.
priya: Thanks. Can we scope this as: tenant opt-in (manual) + scheduled opt-in windows (customer sets peak window)? We should avoid auto-toggle without consent.
devon: Agreed on manual opt-in. From infra: plan is staged traffic steering in the EU region only, with live shadowing for at least one full business day. We should define slices by percent and by tenant size.
laura: Ops ask: define exact health signals for automatic rollback. My suggestion: p95 latency increase > 20% OR end-to-end error rate delta > 0.5% OR quality regression > 1.5% on customer prompt set. Any one triggers immediate failover.
jamie: Good. Also: we need a customer-facing blurb explaining tradeoffs (cost vs small quality variance) and explicit acceptance checkbox in Console. Carla from CS will own consent capture.
carla: I'll draft the wording. Also request per-tenant emergency contact for manual rollbacks.
priya: Feature-flag design: two flags: tenant_opt_in_enabled (boolean per-tenant) and opt_in_warmup_fraction (global double). Also a safety flag: opt_in_force_pinned true/false to instantly route any tenant to pinned variant.
devon: Implementation note: use routing weights backed by the router service. Warmup should ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over configurable windows. Each step waits for gating signals.
ops-bot: canary-runner: scheduled job created -> eu-quant-shadow-1 -> duration:48h -> initiator:devon.
laura: For A/B measurement: run randomized split on identical requests and compute divergence metrics (semantic similarity + token edit distance). We'll need a baseline eval harness.
jamie: Decision on QA triggers: require green on both synthetic eval and live shadow. Synthetic: per-tenant prompt set (minimum 50 prompts) with thresholds. Live: no SLA breach and divergence below threshold for at least 2 observation windows.
priya: Circuit-breaker details: if GPU pool utilization > 80% for 5m OR queue latency > 200ms for 3m -> throttle opt-in ramp and divert new opt-in allocations to premium pool.
devon: Also implement a soft-eviction policy: when a tenant hits the SLA exceptions we shrink their opt-in percentage to 0 and mark them as "cooldown" for 24h. UI shows status + reason.
carla: Are we exposing metrics to customers? They asked for transparency. We should expose opt-in percentage + observed p95 + quality delta in Console.
laura: Yes, but with caveat: quality delta is internal metric derived from our prompt sets. We'll show the number and a link to the evaluation artifact.
jamie: Launch checklist draft: 1) Flag contract + Console control implemented, 2) Canary shadow running in staging + synthetic pass, 3) Live EU shadow for 48h, 4) Dashboard/alerting wired, 5) Customer consent captured, 6) Runbook + rollback ladder published.
priya: Owners: Priya -> flag API + Console controls, Devon -> router + pool fallback, Laura -> eval harness + gating, Carla -> customer comms & consent, Jamie -> final go/no-go.
devon: Timeline: aim to land staging changes by Thu, run 48h staging shadow Fri-Mon, then request customer opt-ins for a controlled pilot next week.
carla: I'll target outreach to the pilot customers today and collect emergency contacts.
laura: Add acceptance criteria for small tenants: for tenants < 5 TPS, require 24h live observation even if slices are green.
jamie: Good call. Any objections?
priya: None from me.
devon: thumbs up.
ops-bot: deploy: feature-flags/eu-optin -> staging -> started by devops-ci.
jamie: I'll draft the rollout playbook doc and link it in the product spec. If no blockers by EOD, start staging run tomorrow morning.
